title: DIC Qualifying Periods Schedule: Veteran's Disability, Marriage and the 8-Year Provision
content:
This schedule sets the periods of disability and marriage that Dependency and Indemnity Compensation (DIC) for a surviving spouse turns on, together with the 8-year provision period. The figures are identical in all six rate categories: DIC Surviving Spouse (Basic Rate), DIC Surviving Spouse (Basic Rate with 8-Year Provision), DIC Surviving Spouse (Housebound), DIC Surviving Spouse (Housebound with 8-Year Provision), DIC Surviving Spouse (Aid and Attendance) and DIC Surviving Spouse (Aid and Attendance with 8-Year Provision).

## Part A — Veteran's total disability before death

| Schedule item | What it measures | Figure (all six categories) |
|---|---|---|
| Total-disability period before death | Years of continuous total disability before death that make DIC payable for a death that is not service-connected | 10 years |
| Total-disability period from discharge | Years of total disability continuously from discharge that make DIC payable | 5 years |
| Former-prisoner-of-war total-disability period | Years of total disability before death that make DIC payable for a former prisoner of war | 1 year |

## Part B — Marriage to the veteran

| Schedule item | What it measures | Figure (all six categories) |
|---|---|---|
| Post-service marriage period | Years after the end of the period of service in which the disability arose within which a marriage qualifies | 15 years |
| Minimum marriage length | Years of marriage before death that qualify a spouse when no other marriage condition is met | 1 year |
| Child of the marriage | Whether a child born of the marriage qualifies the spouse regardless of marriage length | Yes |

## Part C — The 8-year provision

| Schedule item | What it measures | Figure (all six categories) |
|---|---|---|
| 8-year provision period | Years the veteran must have been rated totally disabled immediately before death, while married to the spouse throughout | 8 years |
| Proof from the rating record | Whether the 8-year provision is proven only from the veteran's rating record | Yes — proven only from the rating record |

## Notes to the schedule

1. Part A periods are lengths of total disability; the former-prisoner-of-war figure of 1 year is the shortest of the three and applies only to a veteran who was a former prisoner of war.
2. The post-service marriage period of 15 years is counted from the end of the period of service in which the disability arose, not from the date of death.
3. The minimum marriage length of 1 year is measured as marriage before the veteran's death, and is the marriage condition that applies when no other marriage condition is met.
4. Because a child born of the marriage qualifies the spouse regardless of marriage length, a marriage shorter than 1 year can still qualify where there is such a child.
5. The 8-year provision period of 8 years must fall immediately before the death and the marriage must have lasted throughout it; only the veteran's rating record proves it.

## Hypothetical readings

- A marriage that began 14 years after the end of the period of service in which the disability arose falls inside the 15-year post-service marriage period; one that began 16 years after it falls outside.
- A veteran rated totally disabled for the 8 years immediately before death, with the spouse married to the veteran for all of those years and the rating record showing it, meets the 8-year provision period; 7 years of such a rating does not.
